decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Add a bookmark by URL.” Round 1 client continued with requirements without contesting URL-based saving.
decisions.note: The proposed primary save flow conforms to the reference at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker proposed auto-fetching only “the page title” by default and offered “maybe favicon/description.” Round 1 client supplied the full behavior: “metadata fetching best-effort for the title, description, favicon, and preview image.”
decisions.note: The client corrected the incomplete metadata set at the specification gate; preview-image fetching was not among the offered alternatives.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker proposed an optional title/notes during addition and “Edit … bookmarks.” Round 1 client confirmed that fetched fields should remain editable manually.
decisions.note: The presented pre-save input and post-save editing behavior is consistent with editable bookmark metadata; the response reinforces rather than corrects it.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Organize with tags.” Round 1 client: “Tags should be the main organization method.”
decisions.note: Tag assignment/organization was conforming at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker proposed “filter by tag”; the client retained tags as the main organization method.
decisions.note: Specific-tag filtering is a conforming presented decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker asked whether tags were enough or folders were also needed. Round 1 client instead requested “reusable saved views combining a search with included or excluded tags.”
decisions.note: The client extended the proposed organization scope with the reference-conforming saved-filter concept.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker limited search to “title/URL/notes.” Round 1 client required search to “cover all bookmark text and tags.”
decisions.note: The client corrected the limited search fields, notably adding the omitted description/content scope.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presented ordinary title/URL/note search without phrase syntax. Round 1 client explicitly requested “exact phrases.”
decisions.note: Exact-phrase search was a related missing search behavior supplied by the client.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presented basic search with no Boolean grammar. Round 1 client requested “simple AND/OR/NOT combinations.”
decisions.note: The client surfaced the missing Boolean-search requirement, although its statement did not mention parentheses or the quoted-operator literal rule.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker’s proposed core feature list gave no duplicate-save behavior. Round 1 client requested “duplicate URLs to open the existing bookmark for editing.”
decisions.note: The client added the reference-conforming duplicate convergence rule at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker proposed favorites but no read-later state. Round 1 client explicitly requested “read-later status.”
decisions.note: The client supplied the missing read-later state requirement; favorites are orthogonal and were not treated as a divergence.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker included deletion but no archive behavior. Round 1 client requested “reversible archiving.”
decisions.note: The client added a non-permanent, reversible alternative to deletion at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker’s proposed core scope omitted sorting. Round 1 client explicitly requested “sorting.”
decisions.note: The client supplied the related missing list behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker’s proposed core scope omitted selection and bulk operations. Round 1 client requested “selecting bookmarks for bulk actions.”
decisions.note: The client added the missing multi-select bulk-action behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker did not propose importing. Round 1 client requested “import … of standard browser bookmark files.”
decisions.note: The client added the standard bookmark-import capability.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker did not propose exporting. Round 1 client requested “export of standard browser bookmark files.”
decisions.note: The client added the standard bookmark-export capability.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker’s core proposal omitted preservation. Round 1 client stated, “If practical, preserving a local copy of the linked page is important too.”
decisions.note: Despite the practicality qualifier, this is an explicit request for the related local-snapshot requirement.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker explicitly proposed “delete bookmarks”; the client did not contest deletion and separately requested reversible archiving.
decisions.note: Permanent deletion remained a conforming distinct operation.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker explicitly proposed “Favicon shown per bookmark.”
decisions.note: The recorded per-item favicon display decision conforms to that aspect of the readability-first list requirement; no conclusion is inferred about unpresented layout details.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: “on add, the server fetches title/description/favicon/preview image.” Round 2 client accepted the application as presented.
decisions.note: The revised implementation presentation contains the complete automatic metadata set.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: “all fields stay fully editable,” with a fetch button that fills only empty fields.
decisions.note: The implementation presentation preserves manual control over bookmark fields and fetched metadata.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker described snapshots uniformly as a “single-file HTML copy of the page” and gave no PDF-download exception. Round 2 client only said the app “covers what I need” and accepted it.
decisions.note: The presented snapshot rule diverges for PDF URLs. The client’s bare final approval neither identifies nor explicitly accepts that difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: “adding an existing URL opens the existing bookmark for editing instead of creating a copy.”
decisions.note: The implementation presentation exactly matches duplicate-save convergence.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker defined saved views as “search query + included/excluded tags + scope + sort.”
decisions.note: This conforms to the reusable bundle/saved-filter requirement.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presented “Search over all text and tags via SQLite FTS5.”
decisions.note: The stated full-text search scope conforms; indexing tags in addition is harmless.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker said tags were searchable but enumerated syntax without the required `#tag` form. Round 2 client gave only general final approval.
decisions.note: General tag indexing is not the specified `#tag` query behavior, and the client did not surface that difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker enumerated “implicit AND, OR, and NOT/-term exclusion” but did not present parenthesized groups or the rule that quoted operators become literals. Round 2 client accepted without mentioning either difference.
decisions.note: The implemented-search presentation remained narrower than the fixed Boolean grammar; bare approval is not accepted divergence.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker explicitly presented support for “exact phrases.”
decisions.note: Exact quoted-phrase matching conforms at implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presented multi-select bulk actions for read-later, tags, archive/unarchive, and delete.
decisions.note: Selection of multiple bookmarks and the required classes of bulk action conform.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker called selection “Gmail-style select-all” but did not state whether it applies to every bookmark matching the current search/tag/perspective filter. Round 2 client gave only general approval.
decisions.note: The presentation does not establish whether whole-collection selection is correctly bounded by the current filter, and the response does not clarify it.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker listed newest, oldest, recently updated, and title A–Z/Z–A sorting.
decisions.note: Multiple date/title sort keys conform.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presented Netscape HTML import, folder-to-tag mapping, Firefox tags, and duplicate merging, but did not state whether `date added` is preserved. Round 2 client gave only general approval.
decisions.note: The format and tag behavior are established, but evidence cannot determine conformity with the required date-preservation rule.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker explicitly presented export in “standard Netscape browser bookmark HTML.”
decisions.note: The export format conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presented a bookmark “read-later” state and read-later bulk action.
decisions.note: The recorded ability to mark bookmarks for later reading conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker separately presented reversible archive state, archive/unarchive actions, and delete.
decisions.note: Archive is explicitly reversible and distinct from deletion.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker listed bookmark “notes” but did not say that notes accept Markdown or are rendered when viewed. Round 2 client gave only general approval.
decisions.note: The presentation establishes note storage but leaves the Markdown behavior indeterminate.
